title: Etale transfer of a concentrated supported normal-slice comparison
statement:
Fix the finite datum $k,\ell,E,n,A$ of [def-pur-conventions], with $n\geq1$, and $b\geq0$. Put $N=\mathbf A^b_k$ and let $0\hookrightarrow N$ be the origin [def-sbc-affine-space]. Let $B$ be any affine $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], put $P=\mathbf A^b_B$, let $C=B\hookrightarrow P$ be its zero section, and write $p:P\to N$ for projection on the normal coordinates [def-pc-base-change]. Let $e:T\to P$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], put $Z=C\times_PT$, and let $\bar t$ be a geometric point on $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For each $r\in\mathbf Z$, write $L_{r-b}=A(r-b)(k)$, using the twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and use the ordinary small-etale supported kernel $Q_C,Q_Z$ and derived supported germ comparison of [def-pur-etale-coordinate-support], with global supported sections [def-pur-support-cohomology] and bounded-below derived functors [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Assume the following concentration data: the field complex $K_r=R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(N,A(r))$ and every supported stalk $(RQ_C(A_P(r)))_{\bar x}$ for $\bar x$ on $C$ have cohomology only in degree $2b$; their degree-$2b$ identifications with $L_{r-b}$ are induced respectively by the ordered coordinate Cartier-Kummer class on $N$ and its supported pullback along $p$, tensored with $L_{r-b}$. The coordinate classes and coefficient tensor/dual identifications are those of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map, def-pur-supported-cup, lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Then the normalized derived supported germ morphism is an isomorphism
$$K_r\longrightarrow (RQ_Z(A_T(r)))_{\bar t},$$
and its degree-$2b$ map is the identity of $L_{r-b}$ under these identifications. Its inverse is the isomorphism obtained by the two functorial good-truncation identifications with $L_{r-b}[-2b]$. Etale restriction gives the canonical identification $e^{-1}RQ_C(A_P(r))\simeq RQ_Z(A_T(r))$, normalized by the literal equality of the support kernels on etale test objects. The isomorphisms commute with further etale restriction, restriction to affine base opens, and with the identifications $A(r)=A(b)\otimes_A A(r-b)$ whenever the input concentration data use these same identifications; this includes negative twists via evaluation of dual powers. In particular, compatible input data on two affine neighbourhoods give the same supported germ isomorphism after their common refinement. For $b=0$ the empty coordinate product is the unit and the assertion is the usual coefficient-line germ identification.

source.place: Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support), kernel definition and support localization; agent conditional transfer lemma extracted from coordinate-model Steps 5--7, using literal etale restriction, injective restriction, normal coordinate pullback and functorial good truncation. Purity/concentration are explicit hypotheses, not attributed to the tag.

proof.text: For any $A_P$-module sheaf $F$ and any etale test object $W\to T$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identifies $(e^{-1}F)(W)$ with $F(W\to P)$. The identification respects the $A$-action: restriction applies the very same action maps, using the constant-ring identification of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The inverse-image closed set on $W$ is both $W\times_TZ$ and $W\times_PC$. Thus the two support kernels are literally the same submodule $\ker(F(W)\to F(W\setminus(W\times_PC)))$. The equality commutes with every restriction map in $W$ and with morphisms $F\to G$, giving $e^{-1}Q_CF=Q_Z(e^{-1}F)$ with the same kernel inclusions. This is the normalization in [def-pur-etale-coordinate-support], not an unspecified automorphism of a support functor.

source.place: Tags 03S2 (section-extension-by-zero, restriction paragraph) and 09XP (section-cohomology-support, support subsheaf)

proof.text: Choose a bounded-below injective resolution $A_P(r)\to I^\bullet$. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] make $e^{-1}I^\bullet$ an injective resolution of $A_T(r)$, with the coefficient identification of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Apply Step 1 termwise: $e^{-1}Q_CI^\bullet=Q_Ze^{-1}I^\bullet$. The two sides represent $e^{-1}RQ_C(A_P(r))$ and $RQ_Z(A_T(r))$, respectively. This derives the specified kernel equality. Put $\bar x=e\bar t$ and $D_r=(RQ_Z(A_T(r)))_{\bar t}$. The natural pullback-stalk identification [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar], applied termwise, identifies $D_r$ with $(RQ_C(A_P(r)))_{\bar x}$. The exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] also applies to $A$-modules, since the action on the stalk is induced on the same kernels and quotients. Hence the assumed concentration and degree-$2b$ identification at $\bar x$ give those at $\bar t$. No finiteness property of $B$ is used.

source.place: Tags 09XP, 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback); module restriction uses sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact)

proof.text: Write $q=2b$ and let $c_N\in H^q_{\{0\}}(N,A(b))$ be the ordered coordinate class in the hypotheses. The normalized germ map $\gamma_r:K_r\to D_r$ of [def-pur-etale-coordinate-support] is derived from restriction to the inverse-image support followed by the ordinary germ map. Its map on a supported cocycle is therefore the germ of the pulled-back cocycle. By [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality], pullback respects Kummer classes, localization boundaries, their ordered supported cup product, and composition. Consequently $H^q(\gamma_b)(c_N)$ is exactly the germ of $e^*p^*c_N$, under the kernel normalization of Steps 1--2. For $v\in L_{r-b}$, the same construction and the tensor/evaluation comparisons of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] give $H^q(\gamma_r)(c_N\otimes v)=\operatorname{germ}_{\bar t}(e^*p^*c_N\otimes v)$. This fixes the scalar and the order; no change of coordinates or sign permutation is made.

source.place: Tag 09XP (supported cocycles); supported cup naturality as formulated in lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality from sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0FPL/0FPM

proof.text: Let $u_K:L_{r-b}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(K_r)$ and $u_D:L_{r-b}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(D_r)$ denote the orientation identifications in the hypotheses, the second transported by Step 2. Their defining formulas are $u_K(v)=c_N\otimes v$ and $u_D(v)=\operatorname{germ}_{\bar t}(e^*p^*c_N\otimes v)$. Step 3 says $H^q(\gamma_r)u_K=u_D$. Thus $u_D^{-1}H^q(\gamma_r)u_K=1_{L_{r-b}}$. This uses every coefficient $v$, so it does not require choosing a generator of the twist line.

source.place: Tag 09XP, with the explicit input orientation identifications

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-good-truncation-exact-normalization] to the ordinary derived category of $A$-modules and the shifted objects $K_r[q]$, $D_r[q]$. Both have cohomology only in degree zero by the hypotheses and Step 2. Shift its natural truncation isomorphisms back and compose with $u_K^{-1}[-q]$, $u_D^{-1}[-q]$ to obtain $a_K:K_r\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{r-b}[-q]$ and $a_D:D_r\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{r-b}[-q]$. The lemma applies to the actual derived morphism $\gamma_r[q]$, not just to a chosen chain map, and its naturality and Step 4 give $a_D\gamma_r=a_K$. Hence $\gamma_r=a_D^{-1}a_K$ is an isomorphism and its inverse is $a_K^{-1}a_D$. These are precisely the two good-truncation identifications required by the statement. The lemma also says that maps between these concentrated objects are determined by $H^q$, a fact used below.

source.place: Tag 0118 (section-truncations), specialized through the existing good-truncation normalization lemma

proof.text: For a further etale map $V\to T$, or the restriction $B_0\hookrightarrow B$ to an affine open and the corresponding restriction of $P$ and $T$, the kernel calculation of Step 1 is unchanged: on each common test object the section and its restriction to the complement are identical. Its composition with a second restriction is again that same map. The normalized supported germ comparisons commute with these restrictions by [def-pur-etale-coordinate-support]; [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] identifies the restricted coordinate class with its pullback. Apply the naturality of [lem-pur-good-truncation-exact-normalization] to the resulting maps of concentrated stalk complexes. In degree $q$ the squares are the identity on the same coefficient line by Step 4; faithfulness on concentrated objects makes the derived squares commute. Inverting these commuting isomorphisms gives the same compatibility for their inverses.

source.place: Tag 09XP (restriction of supported sections), with homology.tex Tag 0118 normalization

proof.text: For twist compatibility use the specified $A(r)=A(b)\otimes_A A(r-b)$ in the input data. [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] makes pullback commute with tensor products and evaluation, including dual powers for negative integers. [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] makes the coordinate class obey the same tensor comparison. Therefore the degree-$q$ comparison sends $c_N\otimes v$ to its pulled-back germ for every $v$, just as in Step 3. When the input concentration data use these coefficient identifications, their induced squares on degree-$q$ cohomology commute. The bijection on morphisms in [lem-pur-good-truncation-exact-normalization], shifted by $q$, then proves the squares for the germ isomorphisms and the truncation inverses. This uses exactly the coefficient comparisons specified in the hypotheses; in particular evaluation for a negative twist introduces no shift and no extra sign.

source.place: Tag 03PK (section-kummer), with the tensor/evaluation and truncation lemmas explicitly cited

proof.text: On a common etale refinement of two affine neighbourhoods with compatible input data, Steps 1 and 6 identify the support kernels and the germ morphisms; their degree-$q$ orientation maps agree by compatibility of the input. Step 5 consequently gives the identical formula $a_D^{-1}a_K$ on that refinement. For $b=0$, $q=0$, the coordinate class is the empty product $1$, both support functors have full support, and the normalized germ map sends $1\otimes v$ to $v$. Steps 4--5 become the degree-zero coefficient-line germ identification. Empty $B$ or $Z$ gives no geometric point $\bar t$ and hence no instance to check.

source.place: Tag 0118, degree-zero case; specialization of Steps 1--7
